building.address: 1234 North Hill Terrace NW, Calgary, Alberta
building.name: North Hill Terrace

evidence.quote: BE IT RESOLVED that a special assessment of $8,500 per unit ($714,000 in total) be levied, payable in four quarterly installments of $2,125 commencing July 1, 2026.
$4,250 remains payable in two quarterly installments of $2,125 (January 1 and April 1, 2027). The installments run with the unit on sale.

flags.explanation: Owners voted 71% in favour of a $714,000 special assessment to replace the parkade membrane. It is payable in four quarterly installments of $2,125 starting July 1, 2026. The unit information statement shows $4,250 still owing on a typical unit, and these installments run with the unit on sale — a buyer inherits the remaining payments.

money_exposure.basis: $8,500 x 84 units = $714,000 (per AGM resolution); $4,250 remains owing per unit per information statement

flags.title: $8,500/unit special assessment levied for parkade membrane

evidence.quote: The reserve fund balance at year-end was $745,000 against a study-recommended balance of $1,221,000 — approximately 61% funded.

flags.explanation: The reserve fund holds $745,000 against a study-recommended $1,221,000 — about 61% funded. The study itself rates 70%+ as 'good', so this building sits below that bar. Underfunded reserves are the single best predictor of future special assessments, and the board is already raising contributions 12% per year through 2029 to catch up.

money_exposure.basis: ($1,221,000 - $745,000) shortfall / 84 units = ~$5,667 per unit to reach the recommended level

flags.title: Reserve fund at 61% of recommended level

evidence.quote: The preliminary opinion of probable cost is $1,150,000, which is not currently funded in the reserve fund plan.
Building envelope remediation 2028-2029 $1,150,000 (preliminary) NOT YET FUNDED

flags.explanation: An August 2026 engineering assessment found deteriorated sealant and cladding failures on the east elevation and recommends full remediation within three years at a preliminary cost of $1,150,000. The reserve fund plan explicitly lists this project as 'NOT YET FUNDED'. With reserves already at 61%, this is a strong candidate for the next special assessment — roughly $13,700 per unit if levied the same way.

money_exposure.basis: $1,150,000 / 84 units = ~$13,690 per unit if levied as a future special assessment

flags.title: $1.15M envelope remediation identified but not funded

evidence.quote: The window water-ingress claim affecting units 304, 305 and 406 remains in mediation; the next session is scheduled for October 28, 2026.

flags.explanation: The corporation is in mediation over a window water-ingress claim affecting units 304, 305 and 406, with the next session set for October 28, 2026. Counsel says no provision is required yet, but active construction-defect disputes can drag on and sometimes end in settlements funded by owners. Worth a direct question to the seller's lawyer about exposure.
flags.title: Window water-ingress claim in mediation (3 units)

evidence.quote: The deductible has increased to $100,000 per occurrence following the June 2024 hail claim ($380,000 paid).

flags.explanation: Following a $380,000 hail claim in June 2024, the corporation's per-occurrence deductible jumped to $100,000 and the annual premium rose 18% to $96,400. If another major claim hits, owners can be assessed for the deductible. The information statement advises buyers to carry a unit owner's policy covering this deductible exposure.
flags.title: Insurance deductible raised to $100,000 after hail claim

evidence.quote: The Board reviewed a draft amendment that would cap rentals at 15% of units (22% of units are currently rented).

flags.explanation: The board will ask owners at the 2027 AGM to cap rentals at 15% of units, while 22% are rented today. If you are buying as an investor — or might rent the unit out later — this directly affects you. Existing rentals are often grandfathered, but the documents do not say so; confirm with the corporation.
flags.title: Proposed rental cap: 15% (22% of units currently rented)

evidence.quote: Unit 1204: fourth noise complaint in six months (late-night music). The Board authorized a final warning letter; fines under section 12.4 of the bylaws will apply to any recurrence.

flags.explanation: Unit 1204 has drawn a fourth noise complaint in six months (late-night music) and received a final warning letter, with fines to follow on recurrence. One problem unit does not define a building, but if you are considering a nearby unit it is worth knowing how the board enforces its bylaws.
flags.title: Repeat noise complaints about unit 1204

money_exposure_basis: $4,250 remaining special-assessment installments per unit + ~$13,690 pro-rata share of the unfunded envelope project
questions_for_realtor_lawyer: Can the seller credit or clear the $4,250 in remaining special-assessment installments at closing?
What is the board's funding plan for the $1.15M envelope remediation, and when will owners vote on it?
What is the status of the window water-ingress mediation, and could a settlement result in owner assessments?
If I might rent the unit in future, would the proposed 15% rental cap grandfather existing owners?
Does my unit owner's insurance policy cover the $100,000 corporation deductible exposure?
summary: North Hill Terrace's documents tell a clear story: a major parkade project is being paid through a levied $8,500/unit special assessment, reserves sit at just 61% of the recommended level, and a $1.15M envelope remediation is on the horizon with no funding plan. Add active litigation and a spiked insurance deductible, and a buyer should price in roughly $17,940 of known or likely near-term exposure per unit.
